headline: Aarti Surfactants Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Aarti Surfactants Limited has filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure under the SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011, signalling a substantial acquisition of shares or an impending change in control; specific acquirer identity, price and quantum remain undisclosed in the public notice.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosure typically precedes a formal takeover announcement, triggering mandatory tender offer obligations and public shareholding reconstitution rules - partners should monitor the BSE/NSE for the detailed Regulation 35 letter and Form 'G' once the acquirer makes its formal announcement within 4 working days.
detail: Aarti Surfactants Limited, a publicly listed surfactant and specialty chemical manufacturer, has submitted a Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE, indicating that a person or group has crossed or is crossing a threshold requiring public disclosure under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Regulation 31(4) is a 'no-objection-required' advanced notification filed by the acquirer to the exchange before formal announcement; it typically precedes Regulation 35 (formal takeover announcement) by 1–4 working days. The disclosure does not include the acquirer's identity, offer price, number of shares, or the nature of the transaction (voluntary or mandatory offer) - all of which are to follow. This stage is critical: the target must now prepare for mandatory general offer obligations, escrow arrangements, and regulatory approvals (Sector-specific: nil for surfactants; general: share-transfer pricing, listed-company takeover rules).

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 31(4)
framework.note: Acquirer's obligation to file advance notification to stock exchange before formal announcement; triggers 4-working-day window for Regulation 35 formal letter.
Formal takeover announcement specifying offer price, number of shares, consideration, and conditions; mandatory within 4 working days of Regulation 31(4).

framework.ref: SEBI Takeover Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 36–37 (Mandatory General Offer)
framework.note: If acquirer acquires or proposes to acquire 25% or more, must make a mandatory general offer to all public shareholders at the highest price paid in prior 12 months.
Permitted exemptions (intrinsic-value cases, preferential allotments, rights issues) may apply; acquirer must seek prior exemption before announcement if relying on these.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 - Section 230 (Court-supervised Merger) & Section 391 (Scheme of Arrangement)
framework.note: If transaction involves merger or scheme, additional approval by NCLT / shareholders required; takeover-only does not trigger.

framework.ref: Listing Agreement / Stock Exchange Rules (NSE / BSE)
framework.note: Target must comply with mandatory disclosure requirements, board committee procedures, independent director approvals, and material subsidiary rules.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 / RBI FDI Policy
framework.note: If acquirer is foreign entity, FDI pre-approval mandatory; surfactant sector generally unrestricted.
If combined enterprise turnover exceeds ₹2,500 cr or acquirer exceeds ₹1,000 cr, CCI pre-merger notification (Form I) required.

conditions: Regulation 31(4) advance disclosure filed to NSE; Regulation 35 formal letter and offer details (price, quantity, conditions) due within 4 working days
Satisfaction of public shareholding requirements (minimum 25% for listed company post-offer, unless exemption granted)
CCI approval if thresholds crossed (combined turnover ₹2,500 cr+)
Regulatory approvals for sector (if any; surfactants generally unrestricted)
Statutory and shareholder approval if scheme or merger contemplated
approvals: SEBI clearance (regulatory review of offer terms, compliance with Takeover Code)
Stock Exchange (NSE/BSE) listing compliance and disclosure clearance
structure.novel: Regulation 31(4) advance notification mechanism allows acquirer to 'test the waters' with exchange before formal announcement, reducing execution risk; however, the 4-working-day clock to Regulation 35 is strict and breach can trigger regulatory action.

triggers.note: Threshold-based: 25% (mandatory general offer), 5% (disclosure), any acquisition of 5% + 1 share triggers reporting.
CCI notification mandatory if combined turnover >₹2,500 cr or acquirer >₹1,000 cr.
Related-party transaction rules, board committee approvals (if acquirer is related party), and disclosure norms kick in post-announcement.

firms.note: No legal counsel names disclosed in the Regulation 31(4) advance notification filing (typical for this stage; counsel names appear in Regulation 35 formal letter).
